qs.q: An abnormal increase in red blood cell count is characterized by which of the following terms?
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an abnormally high concentration of red blood cells in the blood.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - June 12, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in the red blood cell count is characterized by which of the following terms?
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an abnormally high red blood cell count, often leading to increased blood viscosity.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - June 5, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in red blood cell count is characterized by:
qs.e: Polycythemia is a condition characterized by an abnormally high concentration of red blood cells (erythrocytosis) in the blood.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - May 15, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in red blood cell count, often leading to increased blood viscosity and potential for clot formation, is clinically characterized by which of the following terms?
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an increase in the total red blood cell mass, leading to a higher hematocrit and increased blood viscosity.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - May 1, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in the red blood cell count is known as:
o: A decrease in red blood cells (anemia)
A decrease in white blood cells (leukopenia)
An increase in red blood cells (polycythemia)
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an increased concentration of hemoglobin and/or RBCs.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - April 10, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in the total red blood cell count and hemoglobin concentration is known as:
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an increased concentration of erythrocytes in the blood.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - April 3, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)

qs.q: An abnormal increase in the total red blood cell count in the circulation is termed:
qs.e: Polycythemia refers to an increased concentration of hemoglobin and/or RBC mass.
qs.s: Weekly Year 2: Cellular Immunology Exam - March 13, 2026 (Section A: MCQs)
